archetype.name: Game Manager (spot-duty backup)
archetype.definition: A short-area, rhythm passer who keeps the offense on schedule with completions under 10 yards and rarely pushes the ball. He is serviceable in relief, but his margin vanishes when he has to drive throws into the intermediate windows.

report.headline: Steady underneath, turnover-prone in the middle: a usable backup, not an answer
report.take:
Bagent is the Bears' QB2 again. Caleb Williams took the job back in Week 6 after a stretch in which Case Keenum and then Bagent filled in. Bagent's 2026 consists of three appearances: 14% of the snaps in relief against Minnesota, a full game against the Jets after taking over from Keenum, and his lone start, a 7-31 loss at Green Bay. That is 64 attempts, far too few to rank him seriously, but enough to see the outline of the same quarterback we saw in 2023.

The outline is a throw-it-short distributor. His intended air yards sit at 6.02, and on average he throws 1.93 yards short of the sticks. In 2023 his aDOT was 6.2 and his success rate ranked 18th of 66 despite a below-average EPA. Short throws are where he earns his keep. On 0-9 yard attempts he completes 72.4% with a 5.6 CPOE and +0.23 EPA per play, which is good starter-level efficiency. The Jets game showed the best version of this: 25 of 34, 268 yards, +7.9 EPA, with almost no pressure (5.6% pressured). With clean pockets and a game plan built on quick completions, he can run Ben Johnson's offense well enough to win.

The damage comes in the 10-19 yard band. There he is 41.2% with a -13.8 CPOE and all three of his interceptions, worth -7.6 EPA on 17 throws. That is the whole gap between a passable line and a bad one. The Green Bay start was the extreme case: a 23.8% bad-throw rate, two picks, and -0.448 EPA per dropback. Several other numbers sound alarming but deserve less weight. His 40% pressure-to-sack rate ranks 35th of 37, yet it rests on a handful of pressured dropbacks, and in 2023 he ranked 4th of 66 at avoiding sacks under pressure. The zero touchdowns and the ugly red-zone line (-0.339 EPA, 46.7%) come from 16 plays. The target split is noisy too. Rome Odunze turned 12 targets into +7.0 EPA, while Colston Loveland's 14 targets cost -8.2. That reads more like a couple of bad intermediate throws to the tight end than a structural problem.

Where is it heading? Bagent is a backup who protects the ball poorly when he extends his reads, and a capable caretaker when he doesn't. The 17-game pace of 17 interceptions is mostly an artifact of 64 attempts. Still, his interception rate was already middling in 2023, so expect it to settle above the league's 2.2% rather than at it. His value to the Bears is as insurance in a good offense, and the offense around him ranks 7th in success rate.

strengths.title: Efficient, accurate short-area passer
strengths.body: Under 10 air yards he completes 78% with a 5.5 CPOE and positive EPA. Throws of 0-9 yards alone return +0.23 per play. This is the core of his game and matches his 2023 profile of a strong success rate built on a low aDOT. Because it rests on timing and decision speed rather than arm talent, it should hold whenever he plays.

strengths.title: Can run a full game cleanly
strengths.body: His one full, unexpected game against the Jets produced +7.9 EPA on 34 throws with an 8.0 CPOE, and the Bears won 23-12. Kept clean (5.6% pressured), he moved the ball methodically and never let the game get away. That is the realistic ceiling: a functional fill-in who makes the throws the design gives him.

concerns.title: Intermediate throws are where drives die
concerns.body: From 10-19 yards he is 41.2% with a -13.8 CPOE and all three interceptions. That band is a real flaw, not just noise, because it lines up with his limited arm and his tendency to force throws once the quick read is gone. Seventeen attempts is a small sample, but in 2023 he also threw interceptions at a below-average rate while barely attacking downfield. Against defenses that take away the flat, this is the pressure point.

concerns.title: Struggles when he has to start
concerns.body: His only start was a collapse: -0.448 EPA per dropback, a -10.9 CPOE and 9.5% interceptions in a three-score loss at Green Bay. Some of that is one bad afternoon against a division rival with a full week to prepare. It still suggests that when defenses game-plan for him and sit on the short stuff, he lacks the downfield answer.

concerns.title: No red-zone finishing so far
concerns.body: Zero touchdowns on 64 attempts, with red-zone plays at -0.339 EPA and 46.7% completions. Sixteen plays is too few to call a skill problem, and touchdown rates on this little volume swing hard. But a compressed field punishes a quarterback who wins with timing more than velocity, so expect red-zone efficiency to improve only modestly.

trend.note: Three appearances in three different roles: brief relief (-2.8 EPA), a clean full game against the Jets (+7.9) and a poor start at Green Bay (-10.3). Since then he has returned to QB2 behind Williams.

nextGame.headline: QB2 behind Williams; only relevant if he's forced in
nextGame.body:
As of October 20, Bagent is listed as Chicago's QB2 behind Caleb Williams, so he projects to stand on the sideline against New England. The Bears are 3-point home favorites with a 50.5 total. If he did enter, the matchup would suit his short game more than his weakness. New England ranks 19th against short passes and 24th on deep EPA, and it gives up 0.44 EPA per play to opposing WR1s. That favors quick throws to Odunze. The Patriots are stingy with tight ends, though: 3rd in EPA allowed to the TE1, and Bagent's Loveland targets have already gone badly.

Availability: New England has ruled out Carlton Davis III, a 95%-snap corner, and is also missing two depth corners. That thins the secondary any Chicago quarterback would face. On Chicago's side, guard Jonah Jackson (94% of snaps) is questionable with a hip issue, and RB Kyle Monangai is out. Monangai's absence narrows the backfield rotation but does not affect a backup quarterback much.

keyMatchups.title: Quick throws vs thin Patriot secondary
keyMatchups.body: With Davis out, New England's top-corner coverage is weakened, and it already allows 0.44 EPA per play to WR1s. Bagent's best work this year came throwing to Odunze, so if he plays, that connection is the path to efficiency.

keyMatchups.title: Tight end targets into a strength
keyMatchups.body: New England ranks 3rd in EPA allowed to the TE1 and holds tight ends 4 PPR points under their average. That is a bad pairing for Bagent, whose Loveland targets have been his costliest.

nextGame.watch: Whether Williams plays the full game. Bagent only matters if he doesn't.

restOfSeason.body:
Behind a healthy Williams, expect little to no action. If he is pressed into a start, project the Jets version more than the Green Bay version as his median: efficient underneath, around 150-220 yards, with an interception risk above league average because the intermediate game remains shaky. His touchdown rate should climb off zero in any extended run, since that number is mostly sample size. His interception rate should come down from 4.7% but likely stay worse than average. The sack rate under pressure should drift back toward his much better 2023 form.

The environment helps. Chicago's offense ranks 7th in success rate and is coached to scheme quick completions, which fits exactly what Bagent does well. The ceiling is still capped by an air-yards profile that rarely threatens defenses, so even a multi-week starting stretch would look like game management rather than a breakout.
swingFactors: Pass protection with Jonah Jackson banged up

confidence.note: Only 64 attempts across three roles, and he is currently the backup.
